S83.01.note: The comparison is a section of the page, not a dialog; the file has no S83.19 or S83.25, so 25 items are listed.
steps: Open the Pricing page (/pricing), or the plans page reached from Settings > Billing.
Scroll to the section headed "Compare plans".
Read the columns "Plan", "Price", "Billing" and "Usage capacity" and the rows for usage, models, admin and data.
Compare the plans shown with what the Expected line asks for: price, usage and features before choosing.

S83.02.note: The toggle appears only on the Team & Enterprise panel, and only when yearly team checkout is available; it is not on the Individual tab.
steps: Open the Pricing page (/pricing).
Select the "Team & Enterprise" tab.
Click "Annual", then "Monthly" in the toggle beside the seat price.
Look at the price text and the billing line ("billed yearly" or "billed monthly") and compare with Expected.

S83.03.needs: a Free account and a card for the Stripe checkout
S83.03.note: The plan says the owner decision on this item is still open.
steps: Sign in with a Free account, press ⌘, and choose "Billing".
Click "Upgrade plan".
Choose a paid plan on the "Upgrade" page and read the "Upgrade to" dialog.
Click the confirm button and complete the Stripe checkout page.
Return to Billing and check the plan name and status shown under the Billing heading against Expected.

S83.04.needs: a paid account billed through Stripe
steps: Press ⌘, and choose "Billing" with a paid Stripe-billed account.
Click "Switch to a smaller plan".
In the dialog, read the "Price", "Usage" and "Limits" sections.
Read the switch date line and the button "Switch on" or "Switch to" and compare with Expected before confirming.
S83.04.where: Settings > Billing > Switch to a smaller plan

labels.text: Upgrading starts a new billing period today, with credit for unused time on your plan.

S83.05.note: The proration amounts appear only when a paid Stripe charge exists to credit.
steps: Start from a Free account: press ⌘, and choose "Billing", then click "Upgrade plan".
Read the sentence about starting a new billing period and credit for unused time.
Choose a paid plan and open the confirmation dialog.
Read "Total due today" and the "Renews" line and compare with Expected.
S83.05.where: Settings > Billing > Upgrade plan > choose a paid plan

steps: Open "Upgrade plan" from Settings > Billing.
Choose a paid plan and read the order panel.
Look for the "Tax" line and the "Total due today" line.
If the panel says "Tax is calculated at checkout.", note that tax is only added on the Stripe page, and compare with Expected.
S83.06.where: Settings > Billing > Upgrade plan > choose a paid plan

S83.07.needs: a Free account and a valid promotion code
S83.07.note: No valid promotion code was found in the code, so the tester needs one from the owner.
steps: Open "Upgrade plan" from Settings > Billing and choose a paid plan.
In the confirmation dialog, find the "Promotion code" field.
Click "Add a promotion code" and type a code.
Check the discount line shown below the code, such as "% off", and compare with Expected.
S83.07.where: Settings > Billing > Upgrade plan > choose a paid plan > Add a promotion code

S83.08.needs: an account on a trial (or a plan offered with a trial)
S83.08.note: Trial terms appear only when a trial is offered; the code does not show when that happens.
steps: Open Settings > Billing with an account on a trial.
Read the "Free trial" badge and the "Trial ends on" row.
Read the text under the plan name about the trial end date.
Open "Upgrade plan" and choose a plan with a trial, then read "Your free trial ends on" and the charge after it, and compare with Expected.
S83.08.where: Settings > Billing (status row "Trial ends on" or badge "Free trial")

S83.09.needs: a Free or paid account with no saved card
S83.09.note: The button opens the Stripe billing portal, not an in-app card form.
steps: Press ⌘, and choose "Billing".
Find the "Payment" heading.
If no card is saved, click "Add payment method".
Complete the card form that opens and compare the new card with Expected.
S83.09.where: Settings > Billing > Payment > Add payment method

S83.10.needs: a saved card on a paid or Stripe-billed account
S83.10.note: Removing or changing a card happens in the billing portal; no remove control was found in the app code.
steps: Press ⌘, and choose "Billing".
Under "Payment", read each saved card line with its "Default" badge and "Expires" date.
Click "Manage cards" to change or remove a card in the billing portal.
Compare the default card, update and remove options with Expected.

S83.11.needs: a paid checkout or a Stripe billing portal session
S83.11.note: The billing address form is collected on the Stripe checkout page (tax-policy.ts sets billing_address_collection to 'required'); I found no in-app billing address field, and searched apps/web for 'billing address'.

S83.12.needs: a business buyer account and a paid checkout
S83.12.note: Tax identifier collection is enabled on Stripe checkout (apps/web/lib/billing/tax-policy.ts); I found no in-app tax ID field, and searched apps/web for 'Tax ID' and 'VAT'.

S83.13.needs: a Free account and a completed paid checkout
S83.13.note: The heading in the code is written with an HTML entity for the apostrophe.
steps: Complete a paid upgrade on the Stripe checkout page.
Return to the app; it opens Billing with success in the address.
Wait for the page to update the plan.
Read the heading "You're all set." and the plan name beside it, and compare with Expected.
S83.13.where: Finish a paid checkout > Billing > You're all set.

labels.text: Your last {planLabel} payment didn’t go through

S83.14.needs: a paid account with a failed renewal
S83.14.note: The notice is shown only for past-due or unpaid Stripe-billed plans.
steps: Use an account whose renewal failed, press ⌘, and choose "Billing".
Read the red notice at the top of the page.
Read the text "Your last ... payment didn't go through" and the status "past due" or "unpaid".
Check that the notice shows how to fix it with the buttons "Pay" and "Update payment method", and compare with Expected.

S83.15.needs: a paid account with a failed payment
S83.15.note: The payment-failure page button "Open billing" leads to /settings/billing.
steps: Use an account with a failed payment and open Settings > Billing.
In the red notice, click "Update payment method" (or the "Pay" link for the open invoice).
Complete the payment in the billing portal or on the invoice page.
Return to Billing and check that the notice is gone and the status is active, as Expected says.

S83.16.needs: a paid account with invoices and credit purchases
S83.16.note: A Free account shows only empty-state text; the invoice list is also at /billing/invoices.
steps: Press ⌘, and choose "Billing".
Scroll to the "Invoices" heading and read the table.
Scroll to the "Credit history" heading and read its rows.
Compare the lists with Expected: past bills and credit purchases.
S83.16.where: Settings > Billing > Invoices (and Settings > Billing > Credit history)

S83.17.needs: a paid account with an issued invoice
S83.17.note: The Settings link opens the hosted invoice page; the PDF file link is on the invoices page.
steps: Open Settings > Billing and scroll to "Invoices".
Find an invoice row with a link labelled "Pay" or "View".
Click the link; it opens the hosted invoice in a new tab.
On /billing/invoices, check the "PDF" link in the "Invoice" column and compare with Expected.

S83.18.needs: an account with at least one credit purchase
S83.18.note: The exact section that shows this table in Settings > Billing was not confirmed; the component's export name in the source is 'n'.
steps: Open Settings > Billing with an account that has bought credits or paid a top-up.
Find the payment history table and its "Receipt" column.
Click the receipt link for a payment.
Check that a receipt exists for each payment, including credit purchases, and compare with Expected.

S83.20.needs: an account with a refund request
S83.20.note: The code uses the status words Processing, Action needed, Refunded, Failed and Canceled, not 'requested'.
steps: Open Settings > Billing and find the "Refunds" table below the payment history.
Read the status shown for each refund.
Compare the status words with Expected: requested, processing, refunded.

S83.21.needs: a paid account billed through Stripe
steps: Press ⌘, and choose "Billing" with a paid Stripe-billed account.
Click "Cancel plan".
Complete the cancellation in the billing portal that opens.
Return to Billing and check the scheduled end date, and compare with Expected.

S83.22.needs: a paid account with a scheduled cancellation
S83.22.note: The button text is built from the plan name, so the visible label is 'Resume' followed by that name.
steps: Use an account with a cancellation already scheduled and open Settings > Billing.
Find the notice that says the plan ends on a date.
Click the "Resume" button in that notice (its label includes the plan name).
Check that the notice disappears and the plan continues, and compare with Expected.
S83.22.where: Settings > Billing > Resume button in the scheduled-cancellation notice

S83.23.needs: a paid account with a scheduled cancellation
steps: Use an account with a scheduled cancellation and open Settings > Billing.
Read the notice that starts "Your ... plan ends on" and the date after it.
Check the "Price" and status rows below the notice, and compare with Expected.

labels.text: You keep {planLabel} features and credits until then. After that, your account moves to

S83.24.needs: a paid account with a scheduled cancellation
steps: Use an account with a scheduled cancellation and open Settings > Billing.
Read the notice under "Your ... plan ends on".
Check the sentence "You keep ... features and credits until then" and what it says happens after: the account moves to Free and chats, projects and files stay.
Compare with Expected.
S83.24.where: Settings > Billing (notice "You keep ... features and credits until then")

S83.26.needs: an account billed through Apple or Google
steps: Use an account whose subscription was bought in the App Store or Google Play.
Open Settings > Billing.
Read the text about the store billing the plan and the button "Manage in the App Store" or "Manage on Google Play".
Click the button, check it opens the store page, and compare with Expected.
S83.26.where: Settings > Billing > Manage in the App Store / Manage on Google Play

labels.text: This account already has an active subscription with our payment provider. Open Billing to manage it, or contact support if your plan is not showing yet.

S83.27.needs: an account that already has an active paid subscription
S83.27.note: The warning text is returned when checkout is refused; I did not confirm the client shows it before purchase.
steps: Use an account that already has an active paid subscription.
Open "Upgrade plan" from Settings > Billing and choose a paid plan.
Read the warning if checkout is refused: "This account already has an active subscription with our payment provider. Open Billing to manage it".
Compare with Expected and check the warning appears before any second charge.
S83.27.where: Settings > Billing > Upgrade plan > choose a paid plan (warning appears when checkout is refused)

S83.28.needs: a Free account for the purchase, or a paid team owner account to change seats
S83.28.note: The Team card title and the exact pricing-page route from Settings were not confirmed; the Upgrade plan link target was not traced past the button. Checkout and upgrade routes exist (apps/web/app/api/checkout/route.ts, apps/web/app/api/upgrade/route.ts) but the seat count is only visible on the pricing page.
steps: Sign in and open Settings, then the Billing tab.
On the plan row, click "Upgrade plan" (shown on a Free plan) or "Adjust plan" (on a paid plan).
On the pricing page, find the Team plan card and its "Seats" number box.
Type a seat count, or use the up and down values, then check the price line changes ("Seats: ... /mo" or "/yr") and compare with Expected.
Continue to checkout and check the seat count shown before paying.
S83.28.where: Settings > Billing > "Upgrade plan" (opens the pricing page), then the Team plan card's "Seats" box; on a plan already owned, "Update seats" is the button

S83.29.needs: a workspace admin account in a workspace with seats, and a second account in the same workspace to assign
S83.29.note: The seat-type control in Settings > Workspace is labelled only by aria-label ("Seat type for ..."), not visible text; the Members page is the route to it per the nav hint "Roles, invitations, seats". How a person first reaches the workspace console from the main screen was not traced.
steps: Sign in as a workspace admin and open the Workspace area.
Click "Members" to see the people list, roles and invitations.
Click "Billing" in the same Workspace area and read the "Plan and seats" section.
Compare the "Seats used" row (for example "N of M") with the members list and the seat assignment controls.
Invite or assign a member and check the seats used count changes.
S83.29.where: Workspace > Members (seat counts appear on Workspace > Billing under "Plan and seats")

S83.30.needs: an enterprise contract on the workspace and an admin account
S83.30.note: The contacts are shown read only; no edit control was found in the component, though the billing-contract API route accepts contact changes.
steps: Sign in as an enterprise organization admin and open Workspace, then Billing.
Scroll to the "Enterprise contract" section (shown only when the plan has a contract).
Read the "Contacts" part.
Compare "Billing contact" and "Procurement contact" with the names on record; a missing one shows the not-on-record text.
Check that these are read only, as the section caption says.
S83.30.where: Workspace > Billing, then the "Enterprise contract" section and its "Contacts" part

S83.31.needs: an enterprise contract with a purchase order number and an admin account
S83.31.note: Offline payment reporting exists only as an API route (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/billing-contract/route.ts, remittanceReference) and the service apps/web/lib/services/enterprise-contracts/invoicing.ts; no UI control for it was found under apps/web/features or apps/web/app. Invoice terms and PO numbers are displayed only.
steps: Sign in as an enterprise organization admin and open Workspace, then Billing.
In the "Enterprise contract" section, read the "Payment terms" and "Purchase order" rows.
Scroll to the "Invoices" section and read the recent invoices, newest first.
Compare the purchase order number and payment terms with the order form on record.
Note that no screen for reporting a bank transfer was found; check whether offline payment reporting is shown anywhere.
S83.31.where: Workspace > Billing, then the "Enterprise contract" section: "Purchase order" row and "Invoices" section

S83.32.needs: a Free account shows the empty state; a paid or top-up account shows purchase rows
S83.32.note: The history lists purchases with other credit types (refund, bonus, adjustment, usage); the Settings route to the Billing tab was taken from the nav label, not traced from the first screen.
steps: Sign in and open Settings, then the "Billing" tab.
Scroll to the "Credit history" section.
Find rows labelled "Top-up purchase" for credit purchases.
Compare each purchase row with the credits bought and the date.
If there are no purchases, the empty text should say "No credit activity yet."
